text:
alex: Quick heads-up — did a narrow profiler pass on the fused-attn path (QKV packing + bias/rope + epilogue fusion) on the latest runtime branch. Seeing a surprising perf regression when KV cache reuse rate is high (~70%+).

maria: Can you paste the numbers and the flags you ran with?

alex: Sure. Ran on T4-equivalent cluster, 4 GPUs, batch shapes mostly 1-4. Flags: `--qkv_pack=true --postproc_inline=true --kv_cache=true`. Results (median latency per token-ish):
```
Scenario                 | seq=32 cold | seq=32 hot-KV | seq=128 cold | seq=128 hot-KV
baseline (no epilogue)   | 3.1ms       | 2.9ms         | 5.8ms        | 5.6ms
fused (epilogue on)      | 2.7ms       | 3.3ms         | 5.1ms        | 6.0ms
% change (fused vs base) | -12%        | +13%          | -12%         | +7%
```
Note: "hot-KV" means steady-state with high KV cache hit ratio. Regression only shows up when cache reuse is high and batch sizes small.

devon: Huh. That smells like extra memory traffic in the fused epilogue when we write back to the KV buffers / reuse slots. Did you capture CUPTI L2/L1 counters or flamegraphs?

alex: Yup — Nsight flamegraph shows a new memcpy-ish hotspot in `epilogue_write_kv()` when postproc is inlined. CUPTI counters: L2 read increase ~1.8x, global load/store increase ~1.4x.

cheng: I suspect our epilogue fusion is doing an extra tiled store to the KV cache for aligned packing, which was fine on cold fills but on hot reuse we end up doing read+modify+write on the same cachelines. Small batches mean poor overlap with compute and the stores serialize.

nora: Could also be kernel selection: the runtime picks the fused kernel for small seq because latency is good without KV, but with KV cache the data movement pattern changes. Maybe we should add a heuristic that disables epilogue fusion when `kv_cache_reuse_rate > X` and `avg_seq < Y`.

maria: Before heuristics, can we reproduce with a toggle? Try `--postproc_inline=false` to move epilogue to separate kernel and see perf.

alex: Did that. With inline disabled:
```
seq=32 hot-KV  : fused (separate epilogue) 2.8ms  (vs 3.3ms with inline)
seq=128 hot-KV : fused (separate) 5.6ms  (vs 6.0ms with inline)
```
So moving epilogue out fixes the regression (~15% improvement). Cold runs still prefer inline.

devon: Ok that supports the in-place write contention theory. Have you checked atomic vs non-atomic store paths? Might be we introduced a write-combine barrier for correctness when packaging QKV + rope and it's killing throughput on reuse.

alex: Investigating atomics now. Also saw that when we disable `qkv_pack` entirely, fused path wins across the board but increases peak memory usage.

perf-bot: Automated microbench summary uploaded: `/bench/fused-attn/1823456789/kernelsummary.json` (CI run). Key note: epilogue-inline shows regressions at reuse >= 0.6 for batch<=4.

cheng: Plan proposal: 1) Add a runtime decision: if `kv_cache_reuse_rate >= 0.5 && avg_batch_size <= 4 && avg_seq <= 64` then prefer non-inlined epilogue kernel. 2) Add a low-overhead perf counter to measure per-route reuse rate. 3) Explore an optimized store path for inlined epilogue that avoids read-modify-write for fully packed kv slots.

nora: +1. Also add a regression test in perf harness that simulates hot-KV reuse so this doesn't slip.

maria: Who wants to own the PR? Small set of changes — heuristic + test.

alex: I'll open the PR this afternoon. Draft name: "runtime: avoid epilogue-inline when kv-cache hot and small-batches". Will include the CUPTI traces and the `--postproc_inline` numbers.

devon: If you can, include a microbenchmark that toggles atomic vs non-atomic store to prove correctness/perf tradeoffs. If atomics are the blocker maybe we can redesign the write layout to be append-only for hot reuse.

alex: Will do. Adding issue and linking the perf artifacts. Tagging @cheng @nora for review. :thumbsup:

maria: Thanks — good catch. This was subtle but explains some customer reports of tail latency spikes on dedicated nodes using long-lived KV caches.

perf-bot: Created perf issue #3142 and attached CI artifacts.
